newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt sentences four militants to death for attacks.
newsitem.headline: Egypt sentences four militants to death for attacks.

text.p: An Egyptian military court on Sunday sentenced four Moslem militants to death on charges including throwing bombs outside a cinema, shooting dead a police colonel and attacking a bus carrying Austrian tourists.
Judge Faisal Heybae also sentenced 13 of 19 defendents to between five years and life in prison. Two were freed.
The 19 defendants, including two juveniles, were also charged with belonging to Egypt's largest militant group, the Gama'a al-Islamiya (Islamic Group).
Eight Austrians and eight Egyptians were wounded in December 1993 when militants threw two bombs and fired shots at their bus near Cairo's ancient Amr ibn el-As mosque.
Days earlier, militants had attacked a cinema in a Cairo suburb of Helwan as crowds were leaving, killing the policeman on guard and wounding six people.
The public prosecutor had said in October the men killed police Colonel Ahmed Shalaan outside his home in Cairo in 1994 and they had attempted to assassinate other key political figures.
